name: MyoChallenge
ability_definition: The ability to quickly move your hand, your hand together with your arm, or your two hands to grasp, manipulate, or assemble objects.

task_realism.reasoning: Die reorientation is close to a real sub-skill: turning a small part in the hand to a target pose before inserting or inspecting it. Rotating Baoding balls is a stylized exercise with no direct workplace equivalent. Neither track involves reaching, grasping, placing or assembling objects, which are the core of workplace dexterity tasks like assembly-line work, packing or tool handling.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Testing happens entirely in MuJoCo simulation with privileged state observations. The physiologically realistic muscle-tendon model adds real actuation constraints, and phase-2 randomization of targets and object properties adds some variation. There is still no real sensor noise, no hardware wear, no cluttered workspace and no consequences for dropping objects. Episode time limits give only a weak stand-in for the speed demands of real work.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The ability covers fast hand, hand-arm and two-handed grasping, manipulation and assembly. MyoChallenge tests only single-hand in-hand manipulation of one or two simple rigid objects. It has no arm transport, no bimanual coordination, no grasp acquisition and no assembly. Speed appears only indirectly, through the Baoding rotation-rate requirement, so the benchmark covers a narrow slice of the construct.

format_match.reasoning: The output is continuous motor control of a hand acting on physically simulated objects. That is structurally the right kind of output for dexterity, unlike multiple choice or text. However, the inputs are low-dimensional state vectors rather than vision or touch, the outputs are muscle activations of a simulated limb, and scoring is a pose-tolerance success rate rather than a completed work product such as an assembled item.

transferability_reasoning: MyoChallenge does exercise genuine contact-rich dexterous control with a biologically realistic hand, which makes it the most faithful dexterity benchmark available in 2022. Its transfer to workplace manual dexterity is still limited. It is confined to simulated single-hand in-hand reorientation of toy objects, with no grasping, arm movement, bimanual work or assembly, and speed is measured only indirectly. Success on it says little about whether a system could quickly assemble or handle real objects on the job.

2022.model_or_system: Team stiff_finger (PPO-LSTM with a curriculum, final ensemble of policies), Baoding Balls track, Phase 2
2022.metric: percent (the challenge's task score, i.e. share of evaluation episodes solved; effort, 0.03, was a secondary measure)
2022.human_reference: General adult workforce performing everyday manual dexterity tasks (in-hand manipulation and object rotation), not specialists such as surgeons or watchmakers
